spatial_entity.notes: Site-level identity for the 1296-1297 eyewitness claim. The modern UNESCO Angkor reference point is a navigation/evidence-locus proxy only; it is not the historical labor-system extent or the political extent of the Khmer Empire.

claim.date_text_original: Zhou Daguan's approximately eleven-month residence at Angkor, 1296-1297
claim.spatial_precision: Angkor/Yasodharapura capital-core eyewitness observation; no empire-wide inference
claim.summary: During his 1296-1297 residence at Angkor, Zhou Daguan described household slaves who were purchased, valued, used in domestic service, punished after escape, and whose children through enslaved mothers inherited slave status. The atlas records a bounded household-slavery claim for the Angkor capital-core during this observation window, without converting Zhou's household generalizations into an empire-wide prevalence estimate.
claim.notes: Derived from the internally reviewed EXP-06 Khmer 1300 synthesis. The claim is limited to the capital/core and the observed period. No P-level, population share, source-region nationality, or full Khmer Empire practice polygon is inferred.

territorial_practice.notes: Concrete purchase, coercion, runaway punishment and hereditary-status features support slavery at the Angkor capital/core. Zhou's prevalence impressions are not census evidence and are not converted into map intensity.

source.title: A Record of Cambodia: The Land and Its People
source.author_or_institution: Zhou Daguan; translated by Peter Harris
source.geographic_scope: Angkor / Yasodharapura and surrounding Cambodian court society
source.independence_notes: One eyewitness textual chain. Later translations, quotations and publisher summaries are not independent observations.
source.reliability_limitations: Foreign observer using outsider social and ethnic categories; surviving text transmitted through later editions. Household-frequency statements are observational generalizations, not a census.

evidence.evidence_role: near-anchor eyewitness description of household slavery
evidence.locator: Chapter 9, 'Slaves': purchase/value, domestic service, runaway punishment and hereditary status through enslaved mothers.
evidence.notes: Use for bounded capital-core presence and institution features, not empire-wide prevalence or modern ethnic identification.

source.title: Sources of Slavery in Ancient Cambodia
source.temporal_scope: Long-run epigraphic and textual evidence, including late Angkorian sources
source.independence_notes: Specialist synthesis of inscriptions and Chinese textual evidence. It is an interpretive layer, not an independent eyewitness for Zhou's 1296-1297 observation.
source.reliability_limitations: Broad diachronic synthesis; it must not be used to project one legal/status pattern uniformly across periods or places.
